# decision(hfp-010): participant names in transcript text on upload

## Task

Decide what happens to participants' real names inside the transcript text when a file is uploaded. ADR 0004 gives speakers pseudonymous `participants.label`s ("P3"), but `transcripts.raw_text` and `segments.text` still keep the names exactly as written, including speaker prefixes like `Ana:` and anything people say about themselves. ADR 0004 records this as a separate privacy decision (Consequences).

This has to be decided before HFP-011. Transcripts never change after upload, so changing the rule once real data exists means a data migration and new transcript versions.

Options to weigh:
- Keep text as uploaded. Pseudonyms apply only in the UI. This is the simplest option, but names stay in the database.
- Replace speaker prefixes with the participant label on upload. Names said inside the text stay.
- Let the researcher review and replace names (a find/replace step) before the transcript is stored.
- Combine one of these with deleting `display_name` when a Participant is deleted.

## Parent Story

Hosted-first pivot (ADR 0001), data model (ADR 0004). Was "Block 2" in `notes/task-list.md`.

## Blocked by

Nothing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The decision is recorded as a new ADR, or as an amendment to ADR 0004, including how it affects `raw_text`, segment offsets and `content_hash`.
- [ ] Any new personal data or processing is documented (CLAUDE.md: document new personal data before shipping it).
- [ ] HFP-011's acceptance criteria are updated to match.
